subject: Edgeware POC: workload profile confirmation & owner commitments
messages:
From: Alex Reiner <alex.reiner@edgeware.io>

Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai, monica_patel@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-04-29T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Intro + POC scope (quick recap)

Thanks for the call this morning, Priyom. Appreciated the clear run-through. Per your ask, here's the current workload snapshot from our side and a short note on what we'd like to validate in the POC:

- Baseline traffic: ~5 RPS sustained (global), mostly during business hours (09:00-18:00 PDT).
- Burst profile: periodic spikes up to ~120 RPS for 60-90s (roughly every 20–30 minutes during peak).
- Typical concurrency: 6–10 concurrent outstanding requests during peak.
- Average prompt tokens: 70–90 (includes user + system context); max observed tokens ~420 for longer threads.
- Typical endpoint: /api/v1/generate-chat (JSON payload with messages array).

I've attached a small traffic sample (anonymized) and a CSV with the minute-level RPS for the last 72 hours. Procurement is CC'd on this thread — they handle PO/DPA routing.

Next steps from our side: confirm test window and share an auth key or allowlist IPs for trial runs.

Alex
Edgeware Systems
From: priyom_das@redwood.ai
To: Alex Reiner <alex.reiner@edgeware.io>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai, monica_patel@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-04-29T09:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Intro + POC scope (quick recap)

Alex — thanks, that profile helps a lot. Quick clarifications so we size the trial correctly:

- The burst cadence you called out (every 20–30m) — is that tied to a specific customer flow or an internal polling job? We want to reproduce the same cadence in synthetic replay.
- For the 420-token max, is that mostly single-turn prompts or multi-turn context?
- Can you confirm whether payloads include attachments/base64 blobs (we'll need different handling)?

Proposed owners on our side: Ben Carter (trial ops / capacity), Monica Patel (telemetry & acceptance).

Suggested trial timeline (tentative):
1) Day 0: access + traffic sample ingestion (share keys / allowlist)
2) Day 1–2: synthetic replay and soak test (replay your 72h sample at scale with burst windows)
3) Day 3: small live routing window (5–10% traffic)
4) Day 4: full live run / acceptance window

Acceptance criteria (proposed):
- 95th percentile token latency for generate endpoints < 250ms
- Error rate < 0.5% for 5xx and 4xx during acceptance window
- No tokenization/regressions vs sample outputs (we'll run N small eval prompts)

I'll attach a short MOP spreadsheet and a simple checklist. Can you confirm procurement contact and whether Edgeware needs a DPA / SOC2 PDF up-front?

Thanks — Priyom
VP, Solutions
Redwood Inference
From: ben_carter@redwood.ai
To: Alex Reiner <alex.reiner@edgeware.io>, priyom_das@redwood.ai
Cc: monica_patel@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-04-29T10:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Intro + POC scope (quick recap)

Looping in a few ops details from my side — we can support the cadence described. Notes / asks: 

- We can run the synthetic replay to reproduce 120 RPS 90s bursts. We prefer a staged ramp (25% / 50% / 100%) so we can validate autoscaling and queueing behavior.
- For concurrency: we'll instrument both connection and token-level concurrency; please flag any per-customer rate limits you expect us to respect.
- Auth: for the synthetic tests we can use a short-lived API key (we'll generate and send a one-time key) or you can provide an allowlist with IP ranges.
- Data: the CSV you mentioned and the sample payloads are perfect — please redact any PII.

Operational owners (confirmed):
- Ben Carter (trial ops lead) — primary contact for runbook/execution
- Monica Patel (telemetry & acceptance) — primary for SLAs/alerts and post-run analysis

Proposed acceptance quantitative checks:
- 95th latency < 250ms (generate-chat)
- Average request CPU/GPU utilization within expected band (we'll share thresholds after initial run)
- Error ratio < 0.5% and no sustained queue growth > 30s

I'll prepare the MOP with the staged ramp and share it back. Can we block a 30-minute sync tomorrow at 11:00 PDT to lock schedule?

— Ben
From: Alex Reiner <alex.reiner@edgeware.io>

Cc: monica_patel@redwood.ai, procurement <procurement@edgeware.io>

Thanks Ben — that plan works for us. Quick answers: 

- Bursts come from an async notification fan-out (customer-initiated) — cadence is semi-regular but can cluster during marketing events. Reproducing 3–4 high bursts per hour is representative.
- The 420-token cases are multi-turn threads (user + assistant + long system context). No attachments in payloads; files are handled off-band.
- Procurement: please send the DPA and SOC2 pdf to procurement@edgeware.io. They prefer DocuSign for standard paperwork.

I'll accept the 11:00 PDT sync tomorrow — Alex (we're +1 on the call)
